content.text:
Do not merge [PR #148](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/148) yet. I found two P1 blockers:

1. **Compact-v1 compatibility breaks.** The [wire version remains `1`](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/960e76776dc3415b61d095f86cb22e98784b574d/internal/sem/compact_snapshot.go#L22-L23), but the encoder [adds a twelfth positional field](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/960e76776dc3415b61d095f86cb22e98784b574d/internal/sem/compact_snapshot.go#L185-L190). An existing v1 reader fails on new truncated snapshots with:
   `relation record arity 12, want 11`
   
   This needs a new compact wire version/cache mode with dual-version decoding, or a v1-compatible encoding.

2. **`neighbors --format json` silently hides truncation.** [`neighborEdge`](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/960e76776dc3415b61d095f86cb22e98784b574d/internal/cli/neighbors.go#L61-L73) copies `Evidence` but omits `WarningCodes` and `EvidenceDropped`. I reproduced raw `edges` output containing `EVIDENCE_TRUNCATED` and `evidence_dropped: 2`, while `neighbors` returned eight entries with neither disclosure—making the partial array look exhaustive.

Otherwise, head `960e767` is mergeable/CLEAN and all 10 checks pass. The full semantic suite and focused merge tests pass; no additional core-provider defects surfaced. Review decision remains empty, with two unresolved Copilot threads. I made no repository or PR changes.

What do you recommend?

I recommend **requesting changes, not abandoning the PR**. The core approach is sound; both blockers are contained.

Fix in this order:

1. Introduce `compact-ndjson` v2, while keeping the decoder able to read existing v1 artifacts. Update the compact cache-mode name accordingly.
2. Add `warning_codes` and `evidence_dropped` to `neighborEdge`, copying them in `edgeForRelation`.
3. Add regressions for:
   - decoding old v1 rows,
   - round-tripping a v2 relation with nonzero `evidence_dropped`,
   - truncated evidence through `neighbors --format json`.
4. Re-run CI, resolve the Copilot threads, and obtain human approval.

I would not merge with either issue outstanding, but I also would not ask for a redesign of the provider logic.
Who is decoding the ndjson though?

Good challenge. The compatibility concern is specifically about **compact-ndjson**, not ordinary NDJSON. I’ll trace its actual decoder call sites and distinguish real consumers from merely documented/public ones.

The evidence supports your skepticism: Entire Brain consumes the ordinary object-per-line NDJSON stream, not the compact format. So the compact-v1 issue is a contract/versioning problem, but I have not found a deployed cross-version consumer that it currently breaks.

content.text: There is one more important consequence of that distinction: Brain’s native-NDJSON reader re-marshals typed relation records, so I’m checking whether it preserves the newly added `evidence_dropped` field or silently strips it.

I had conflated two formats. The actual consumers are:

| Consumer | Format | Impact |
|---|---|---|
| Entire Brain | Ordinary object-per-line NDJSON | It invokes `--format ndjson` in [semantic_stream.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/semantic_stream.go:371). Its typed record in [semantic.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/semantic.go:220) lacks `EvidenceDropped`, so it currently strips that new field while re-marshalling—though it preserves `EVIDENCE_TRUNCATED`. |
| Graphmark | Compact NDJSON v1 | Its decoder requires version 1 and exactly 11 relation elements in [temporal.py](/Users/thomi/Projects/graphmark/graphify-parity/graphify_parity/temporal.py:294). PR #148’s 12-element row will hard-fail there. |
| `snapshot-query` and benchmark preflight | Compact NDJSON | Same-version internal consumers; the PR’s updated decoder handles both 11- and 12-element rows, so these are fine. |
| Records cache | Neither | It stores and replays compact bytes without decoding them. |

So Brain is not decoding compact NDJSON, but Graphmark is. More importantly, Brain has a separate ordinary-NDJSON propagation gap.

My revised recommendation: coordinate three small fixes before merging—teach Brain to preserve `evidence_dropped`, update/version Graphmark’s compact decoder, and carry the fields through `neighbors`.
Do that then

I’ll implement the three fixes as coordinated local changes: `neighbors` propagation in PR #148, native-NDJSON preservation in Entire Brain, and compact-row compatibility in Graphmark. I’ll keep each repository on its own branch/worktree, run focused tests, and won’t push or modify the GitHub PR without a separate request.

I’m taking the coordinated compatibility route: preserve PR #148’s compact-v1 output shape, update the known strict Graphmark decoder to accept the optional twelfth relation field, preserve `evidence_dropped` through Brain’s native-NDJSON filter, and expose both disclosure fields from `neighbors`. I’ll add regressions at each boundary.
